display.purpose: Page h1 and the homepage hero only. Spectral at 500 with relaxed tracking — a text face asked to carry a heading by weight, not by being a display face. The system has no display face.

body.purpose: All prose, held to --measure (42rem) for 65–75 characters. Never mono.

label.purpose: Meta lines, nav, legend, footer, annotations. Azeret Mono, uppercase and tracked when it names a thing; sentence case when it annotates a value.

code.purpose: Inline code and code blocks, usually on --mark. Same mono face as the labels — the instrument's one voice.

breakpoints.name: grid-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: post-card and project-grid both go single-column.

breakpoints.name: figure-scale
breakpoints.purpose: 44rem. Inline SVG figures step their label size from 15px to 24px.

motion.name: scroll-smooth
motion.purpose: The only motion declared. Everything else is a state change with no transition, and prefers-reduced-motion forces it off. The world is a plate, not an instrument panel — nothing here plots in real time.

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: The one pill in the system and the only control on every page. Switches sky/plate and persists the choice. Raised-sky ground, so it reads as a surface sitting on the field.
components.html: <button class="ds-theme-toggle" type="button" aria-label="Dark theme" aria-pressed="true"><svg data-icon="sun" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" width="17" height="17"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4"></circle><path d="M12 3v2M12 19v2M4.2 4.2l1.4 1.4M18.4 18.4l1.4 1.4M3 12h2M19 12h2M4.2 19.8l1.4-1.4M18.4 5.6l1.4-1.4"></path></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-theme-toggle { width: 2.75rem; height: 2.75rem; border: 1px solid var(--rule); background: var(--bg-elevated); color: var(--ink); border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; display: grid; place-items: center; padding: 0; } .ds-theme-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Uppercase mono chrome. Active and hover go to ink, never to a star tint — the frame stays out of the magnitude scale's way.
components.html: HomeWritingProjectsAbout
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.65rem; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.86rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-nav a { padding: 0.8rem 0.35rem; text-decoration: none; color: var(--muted); } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a.is-active { color: var(--ink); }

components.name: Atlas Legend
components.description: The world's own voice at the top of the field: uppercase mono stating real counts of what is plotted. A star atlas always ships one, and it is not decoration — it declares the scale of what you are looking at.
components.css: .ds-legend { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.35rem 1.1rem; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); } .ds-legend b { color: var(--accent); font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Magnitude Mark
components.description: The signature. A plotted dot at the head of a catalogue entry whose diameter derives from a real quantity — reading time — and whose tint is its magnitude class. It is a measurement, not an ornament: a mark that does not encode magnitude is noise.
components.css: .ds-post-meta::before { content: ""; display: inline-block; vertical-align: 0.05em; margin-right: 0.45rem; width: calc(0.32rem + var(--mag, 5) * 0.075rem); height: calc(0.32rem + var(--mag, 5) * 0.075rem); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--mag-tint, var(--accent)); }

components.name: Post Card
components.description: An asymmetric 8.5rem annotation column beside a fluid body, separated by hairlines top and bottom. The meta column carries the magnitude mark. Hover moves the h3 colour and nothing else.

components.css: .ds-post-card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 8.5rem 1fr; gap: 1.6rem; padding: 1.7rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); text-decoration: none; } .ds-post-meta { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--muted); letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-post-card h3 { font-family: var(--serif-display); font-size: 1.55rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.01em; line-height: 1.2; margin: 0 0 0.45rem; color: var(--ink); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--rule); text-underline-offset: 0.18em; } .ds-post-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--ink-soft); font-size: 1.02rem; } .ds-post-card:hover h3 { color: var(--accent); text-decoration-color: var(--accent); }

components.description: A bordered, raised plate — the only tonal step in the system. Square corners, no shadow, mono meta.

components.name: Skip Link
components.description: The only solid star-hot surface in the interface. Parked off-canvas until focused, then it slides in. Its hover is pinned to the ground colour — the global a:hover would otherwise repaint it accent-on-accent.
components.css: .ds-skip { position: absolute; left: -9999px; top: 0; z-index: 50; background: var(--accent); color: var(--bg); padding: 0.6rem 1rem; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.85rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-decoration: none; } .ds-skip:focus { left: 0; } .ds-skip:hover { color: var(--bg); }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: Azeret Mono on the mark ground, square and full-bleed within the measure. Scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping.
components.css: .ds-code { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.6; background: var(--mark); color: var(--ink); padding: 1.1rem 1.3rem; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0 0 1.4rem; border-radius: 0; } .ds-code code { background: none; padding: 0; font-size: inherit; }

components.name: Blockquote
components.description: A 2px star-hot left rule and italic soft ink. The only place a border is thicker than 1px.
components.html: If you want an elegant solution, perhaps you need to hold its hand.
components.css: .ds-quote { margin: 1.8rem 0; padding: 0 0 0 1.2rem; border-left: 2px solid var(--accent); color: var(--ink-soft); font-style: italic; } .ds-quote p { margin: 0; }

narrative.overview:
An atlas is not a picture of the sky. It is a plotted field with a scale, a grid you can read a position off, and annotations that tell you what you are looking at. The marks are measurements, and a mark that measures nothing is not in the book.

This system is built the same way. The ground is a ruled coordinate plate at a 6rem module, the chrome is mono because the chrome is instrumentation, and the catalogue plots each entry at a size derived from its real heft rather than decorating it. Colour is a magnitude scale with three steps — hot, cool, faint — and no fourth tint exists, because a scale that keeps growing stops being one.

It replaced a field-manual world of warm paper and a single oxblood accent. That world was competent and generic: cream ground plus high-contrast serif is the most predictable pairing an interface can reach for, and running two faces that sit on every model's default list is why it read as a template. The atlas is the opposite bet — a cool dark field, a working text face, and meaning carried by measurement.

The world owns the frame and the column stays calm. Grid, mono and plotted marks live in the masthead, the navigation, the legend and the catalogue; the running prose is a plain column at a plain measure in a reading face. An atlas that plots behind its own text is a poster.
keyCharacteristics: A ruled coordinate plate as the ground, ruled at a 6rem module and never an overlay on prose
A three-step magnitude scale — hot, cool, faint — as the only colour, with no accent hue and no fourth tint
A mono/serif split with one job per voice: Azeret Mono measures, Spectral reads
Square everywhere, with two round exceptions, both instruments: the plotted mark and the theme toggle
Structure carried by 1px hairlines and the grid, never by shadow — the system has no shadows at all

rules.name: The Frame Owns The World Rule
rules.body: Grid, mono and plotted marks belong to the masthead, the navigation, the legend and the catalogue. The running column stays plain, at a plain measure, in a reading face. The moment the world reaches into the prose it stops being an atlas and becomes a poster.

rules.name: The Magnitude Rule
rules.body: Colour is measurement, not decoration. Three tints in one scale: hot is the brightest magnitude and nothing else, cool is mid and the default link tint, faint is the least weighty thing in view. A tint that does not encode magnitude is noise, and a fourth tint ends the scale.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Spectral carries the whole page. Weight and size do the separating — 500 for structural headings, 400 for prose. There is no display face; asking a text face for a masthead is how the previous world acquired a second serif it did not need.

rules.name: The Mono Measures Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono never sets running prose or a heading, at any size. It is the instrument's voice: labels, meta, annotations and code. A page whose body text is mono is a terminal costume, not an atlas. Uppercase and tracked when it names a thing; sentence case when it annotates a value.

rules.name: The Tinted Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is never pure black or pure grey. Every ink is tinted toward the ground it sits on — cooled toward the sky in dark (#e9e7db, not #fff), violet-cast on the plate (#14161f, not #000) — so type sits on the field rather than being cut out of it.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn, never cast. Two things that need telling apart get a 1px border, the grid, or a tonal step — not a shadow, not a glow, not a gradient. The system has no shadows at all, so one would be a foreign object.

dos: Do hold prose to --measure (42rem) — the reading column is the product, and the world never touches it.
Do size the magnitude mark from real content; it is a measurement, not an ornament.
Do keep mono out of the prose and out of headings, at every size.
Do declare the field before plotting it: a legend stating real counts opens the catalogue.
Do keep corners square. The plotted mark and the theme toggle are the sanctioned exceptions, and both are instruments.
Do check both grounds — every token has a sky counterpart, and the star tints invert from deep (#8a4f11) to luminous (#f0c674).
Do set uppercase tracked mono when a line names a thing, and sentence-case mono when it annotates a value.
donts: Don't add a fourth tint, a gradient, or a glow — the scale has three steps and that is the system.
Don't introduce shadows or elevation. Separation is drawn, never cast.
Don't use pure black or pure grey; every ink is tinted toward its ground.
Don't set body prose or headings in mono — that is the terminal costume the mode rules refuse on a reading surface.
Don't let the grid compete with the text: if it is visible while reading, it is too strong. --grid sits one hairline off --ground by design.
Don't use a star tint decoratively; a tint that does not encode magnitude is noise.
Don't reintroduce a second serif or a display face. Spectral at 500 is the display voice.
